{"decision":"RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. @ajs, dev_reflow2 hub session, 2026-09-27: "I was going to say we could put the reflow2 there also, but I'm concerned that we don't have all the tools. then again, if I keep this dev_reflow2 at running locally, it would still have all 193 tools."

TODAY: reflow2's design is a local store beside its repository, reached by the hub's child-reflow2 connection with all 193 tools. The combined plan moves it last among the moves (position 11, after flo2's), as dec:idea-a-repo-that-holds-its-design-moves-it-to-a-remote-server-once set.

WHAT THE CONCERN TURNS ON, measured the same night:
- The tools actually missing through api.flo2.io are fewer than 17. Of the 17 flo2 refuses, seven take their evidence from the caller and read nothing on the host (flo2's fact:only-wall-check-of-the-machine-side-tools-reads-files-itself-2026-09-27); flo2 schedules five of them at combined position 2, and the other two are the same kind. What genuinely stays missing is wall_check (it reads the files itself), the seven that read other designs by path (combined position 12), and two that stay off by design.
- ⚠️ "KEEP dev_reflow2 LOCAL WITH ALL 193" ONLY HOLDS FOR DESIGNS WHOSE STORE IS ON THIS MACHINE. The hub reaches each child through that child's own server. A design moved to flo2.io is reached through flo2.io's gateway, and reflow2's local client (`--remote`) forwards to that same gateway, so it gets the same 176 today. A local server cannot serve the full list for a design it does not hold.
- reflow2's own work leans harder on the missing and not-yet-remote pieces than flo2's does: CI runs wall_check against the design, release cuts freeze checksums measured on the build machine (position 10), and the export-based CI gate (position 9).
- 🛑 BOOTSTRAP, SHARPER THAN FOR flo2: flo2.io's engine IS reflow2. An engine release that breaks opening designs would also make reflow2's design, the one you would read to fix it, unreachable from flo2.io.

OPTIONS, NONE CHOSEN:
(a) Keep reflow2's design local for good; flo2.io hosts everyone else's. Cheapest; gives up "one blueprint on a server" for the engine's own design.
(b) Move it where the plan has it (11), once CI, release cuts and wall_check have a remote route.
(c) Move it early and accept the gaps. The largest cost of the three: reflow2's CI and release process depend on exactly what is missing.","kind":"exploratory","name":"OPEN — move reflow2's own design onto flo2.io too, or keep it local where every tool is served?","status":"proposed"}
